title: Improvement of Delta-screening in Germany - Closing the individual gap(s)
summary:
Hepatitis D is a viral infection of the liver that can only occur in people with existing hepatitis B infection. The exact prevalence of hepatitis D in Germany is unclear. Recommendations for the treatment of hepatitis B include testing for hepatitis D. Unfortunately, this testing is not always carried out completely. With this study, we first want to test all patients with evidence of hepatitis B for the presence of hepatitis D and find out how many people with hepatitis D we can still diagnose in this way. In addition, we also want to go beyond the recommendation and test repeatedly, not only with the usual antibody diagnostics, but also directly for the presence of the virus. We also want to evaluate the success of this measure.
The normal procedure after diagnosis of hepatitis B infection is to test all patients for contact with hepatitis D. This test looks for antibodies against hepatitis D and is performed using a blood sample. If this test is positive, a subsequent test is performed directly for the presence of the hepatitis D virus (HDV RNA).

In summary:
HBsAg positive (=hepatitis B positive) -->Anti-HDV test
Anti-HDV negative -->no further testing required
Anti-HDV positive -->HDV RNA test (test for hepatitis D virus; if positive = active infection)

Unfortunately, this testing is not automated and must be actively requested by the treating physicians. We would therefore like to test all patients who have not yet been tested according to this procedure.
To this end, we would like to see whether we can detect new hepatitis D infections that would otherwise have remained undetected due to the low accuracy of the tests by repeating the HDV RNA test (=direct test for HDV virus) or HDV RNA test for patients with liver cirrhosis or elevated liver values with negative anti-HDV tests. In these two situations, no further testing would normally be carried out outside of this study. 
So: 
Anti-HDV positive --> HDV RNA negative --> Repeat HDV RNA test
or
Anti-HDV negative + liver cirrhosis/elevated liver values --> HDV RNA test

In addition, we would like to retest patients who have already undergone anti-HDV testing if their first anti-HDV test was more than 10 years ago.

In summary, the aim of this study is to test for hepatitis D in various ways and to check whether these measures lead to more patients with hepatitis D being identified.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
4 groups:
A) HBsAg positive, no previous anti-DHV test
B) HBsAg positive, anti-HDV test 10 years ago
C) HBsAg positive, elevated transaminases or liver cirrhosis
D) HBsAg positive, anti-HDV positive
Exclusion criteria:
Known HDV co-infection
HBsAg negative
Not capable of giving consent
